task.name: A dispatch refused because the account may not call the model quarantines that model for the rest of the run
task.story_text:
---
depends_on:
  - issue-2950
---
## What
Slice 3 of 3 from the decomposition of #2914. When a provider refuses a dispatch before generating anything because the account may not call the selected model, that dispatch identity is quarantined for the remainder of the run: no later dispatch in that run reaches it, and the run continues on the remaining models. The availability classification (#2949) and the pre-dispatch empty-pool stop (#2950) are the earlier slices and have shipped; this one covers what the router learns *from* a refusal it did not predict.

Quarantine is enforced at the one dispatch seam every agent call already passes through (`run_agent`, where the configured-vs-resolved identity is stamped once per dispatch), not at each call site. Phases, roles and flows are covered because they dispatch through the seam, not because each was edited.

## Why
Availability resolution cannot be perfect: a provider may publish no catalog (unverified), the catalog may lag the provider's actual policy, or the answer may go stale mid-sprint. An explicit refusal is stronger evidence than any prior state. Without quarantine, a sprint meets the identical refusal once per story, paying WORKSPACE, preflight, routing and plan each time. That happened across four stories on 2026-09-04, and again three times on 2026-09-15 when the preflight decomposition assessment was routed to a withdrawn cheap-tier model in three consecutive runs. The existing transient-failure quarantine in `provider_health` is adjacent (reviewer-only, time-windowed, pattern-matched on capacity and rate-limit strings) and does not cover configuration refusals.

Two earlier attempts at this scope escalated in plan review after five plans each (sprint `1b75c9e1294c` on 2026-09-08 against this issue, and sprints `4186e8c6c16a` and `e4e1082e86bc` on 2026-09-15 against the parent #2914, which had been left open after decomposition). Every rejection asked for one more thing the criteria left silent: recognising every provider's refusal wording, surviving a process restart, covering one more dispatch surface. This revision names the one signal forge already classifies, states what happens to everything else, and bounds what "remainder of the run" must survive. The identity it quarantines is the canonical dispatch identity routing already uses (#2949), not a new one.

## Acceptance criteria
- The quarantine trigger is the pre-generation provider refusal the runner layer already classifies with its own structured failure code (shipped under #2913). A dispatch that ends in that outcome quarantines the canonical dispatch identity it was made with, the same identity #2949 resolves availability for, so that provider, transport, runner and endpoint scope are all retained. Quarantine applies whether that identity was previously available or unverified: the refusal converts unverified to unavailable for the rest of that run.
- A refusal the runner layer does not classify as pre-generation is never quarantined. It is logged with the dispatch identity and a bounded, redacted excerpt of the provider's response, sufficient to add a recogniser from the log line without reproducing the failure, and the run behaves exactly as it does today. Unclassified refusals fail open, never closed.
- Quarantine is recorded and enforced at the shared dispatch seam. A quarantined identity requested through the seam is refused before any provider call is made. The identity checked is the identity actually dispatched: when a runner substitutes a fallback model or transport internally, the substituted identity is checked the same way. A dispatch that reaches a provider without passing the seam is a bug in that dispatch and is out of scope here.
- Callers that are not a dev, review or validate phase are covered through the seam with no site-specific code. One test shows a quarantined identity is refused for a non-phase caller (the preflight decomposition assessment is the pinned case, since it is the one that halted three sprints).
- "Remainder of the run" means the lifetime of the sprint or run process that observed the refusal. A process restart within the same sprint may lose the quarantine, and after a restart the same identity may be refused at most once more before it is quarantined again. Persisting quarantine across restarts is not required, and the next run resolves availability afresh (#2949) rather than inheriting a quarantine that may no longer hold.
- A refusal of a quarantined identity is a routing outcome, not an agent failure. It carries a distinct marker so that transient-failure and retry classifiers in any phase never re-dispatch that identity in that run, it is never recorded against the model's capability or adaptive profile history, and it never counts as a dev or review failure for the story.
- Every exclusion a quarantine causes is recorded in the routing decision with a reason naming the refusal that triggered it.
- The story whose dispatch was refused continues on the remaining models where any remain, and stops before further spend, naming the excluded models, where none do, the same outcome #2950 defines for an empty pool.
- The existing reviewer-only transient quarantine in `provider_health` keeps its current behaviour.

## Example
```
  ▸ DEV   gpt-5.4  iter=1
  ✗ DEV   refused before generation — account may not call openai/gpt-5.4/cli under
          codex ChatGPT-account auth (HTTP 400). Quarantined for the rest of run 68aec168166d.
  ▸ DEV   gpt-5.6-terra  iter=1
  ✓ DEV   $0.51  5m 02s
  ... later story, same run, non-phase caller ...
  ⚠ ROUTING  openai/gpt-5.4/cli excluded for preflight decomposition assessment —
             quarantined after pre-generation refusal on issue-2775
  ▸ PREFLIGHT_DECOMPOSITION_ASSESSMENT   gpt-5.5
```

An unclassified refusal, left alone:

```
  ▸ REVIEW   some-model
  ✗ REVIEW   failed (HTTP 400, unclassified) — not quarantined; excerpt: "…model access
             requires organisation verification…" [redacted, 160 chars]
  (retry and classification proceed exactly as today)
```

findings.description: When an API profile falls back from its primary model, a fallback model that was already quarantined for the run is still eligible to receive a provider call, and a refusal from that fallback is attributed to the primary model.
When a failed dispatch result carries configuration RefusalEvidence but lacks the runner's pre-generation failure code, the dispatch seam still records a quarantine for that profile.
When a refusal is unclassified or classified as transient, the dispatch seam returns without emitting a not-quarantined log that names the dispatch identity and a bounded excerpt.

The supposed preflight decomposition assessment coverage parametrizes the caller name but invokes run_agent directly for both cases, so it would pass even if the actual assessment caller stopped using the seam.

findings.description: When an unclassified or transient refusal occurs through a quiet pooled or retry dispatch, no not-quarantined diagnostic containing the identity and response excerpt is emitted.

When an OpenAI API profile without tools receives a pre-generation model-access denial, the SDK exception becomes a generic failed result with no refusal evidence or failure code, so the identity is never quarantined and can be called again.

When the selected DEV identity is quarantined after its first configuration refusal while another routed model remains available, the phase aborts as an infrastructure failure instead of rerouting the story onto that remaining model.

When a resumed DEV or REVIEW run encounters a configuration refusal, no quarantine scope is active, so the refusal is not recorded and later dispatches in that resumed run can reach the same identity.

When the codex CLI refuses a dispatch before generation with the exact stream captured in the repository (HTTP 400 with error type invalid_request_error and a message saying the model is not supported for a ChatGPT account, and no machine code field), the refusal is classified transient and the dispatch identity is never quarantined, so the next story in the same sprint pays WORKSPACE, preflight, routing and plan to meet the identical refusal again.

Any provider exception raised on the API loop's first iteration — a 429, a 500, a dropped connection — is now stamped with the failure code provider_refused_before_generation, so an ordinary transport outage is recorded and reported as a provider refusal that never happened.

The active story name is held in a process-wide list set once per run_task, so when a sprint runs stories concurrently on its worker threads, a quarantine recorded during one story is stamped with whichever story most recently entered run_task, and the operator-facing record and the routing exclusion reason point at a story whose dispatch was not refused.

When a Codex CLI dispatch learns a pre-generation entitlement refusal and the profile has fallback_models, the runner records the quarantine but returns the refused result without trying an eligible fallback unless the provider prose also matches the old fallback text patterns.

When an API-loop dispatch receives a pre-generation HTTP 400 entitlement refusal such as model_not_found, the API runner raises the SDK exception instead of returning a refusal result, so the dispatch seam never records the quarantine.

findings.description: When a pre-generation API rejection has error type invalid_request_error and error code context_length_exceeded, it is treated as an account-access denial and quarantines the selected identity for the remainder of the run.
When an API tool loop receives an unclassified HTTP 400 refusal such as context_length_exceeded, the exception escapes before the dispatch seam can emit the required not-quarantined diagnostic.
When provider refusal detail contains a credential-like value, the not-quarantined routing diagnostic writes that value directly to stderr.

When a first-turn provider call fails with an ordinary request defect that arrives on a denial-shaped status — an oversized prompt returning HTTP 400 with code context_length_exceeded, an invalid tool schema returning HTTP 400 with a null code, or a bare HTTP 403 from a proxy or a mistyped endpoint — the refusal is classified as a configuration refusal and the dispatch identity is quarantined for the rest of the run.

When an OpenAI loop dispatch is rejected on its first turn because the model does not accept the tool request shape, the loop now returns a refusal result instead of raising, so the caller's tool-mismatch handler never runs, the capability-mismatch explanation never reaches the operator, and the model is quarantined for the rest of the run.

When a refusal is learned during a pooled dispatch — the review pool or the plan-review pool, which run their agents on their own worker threads — the quarantine record and the routing exclusion reason name the story as 'unknown' rather than the story whose dispatch was refused.

Every exception raised inside a single-shot adapter call — a rate limit, a gateway error, a connection reset, or a local programming error in the request-building code — is recorded with the failure code that names a provider refusal issued before generation, and that code is now also treated as fallback-eligible, so unrelated failures both mislabel the audit trail and trigger a paid fallback dispatch they previously did not.

The branch changes the tool-free OpenAI single-shot exception path to emit refusal evidence and the pre-generation failure code, but the tests never drive an SDK entitlement exception through that adapter path.
The API loop now catches a first-iteration HTTP 400 entitlement exception before the provider-specific re-raise, but no test drives AgentLoopManager or run_api_agent through that exception path.

finding_registry.description: When an API profile falls back from its primary model, a fallback model that was already quarantined for the run is still eligible to receive a provider call, and a refusal from that fallback is attributed to the primary model.
When a failed dispatch result carries configuration RefusalEvidence but lacks the runner's pre-generation failure code, the dispatch seam still records a quarantine for that profile.

The supposed preflight decomposition assessment coverage parametrizes the caller name but invokes run_agent directly for both cases, so it would pass even if the actual assessment caller stopped using the seam.
When an unclassified or transient refusal occurs through a quiet pooled or retry dispatch, no not-quarantined diagnostic containing the identity and response excerpt is emitted.

When an OpenAI API profile without tools receives a pre-generation model-access denial, the SDK exception becomes a generic failed result with no refusal evidence or failure code, so the identity is never quarantined and can be called again.

When the selected DEV identity is quarantined after its first configuration refusal while another routed model remains available, the phase aborts as an infrastructure failure instead of rerouting the story onto that remaining model.

When a resumed DEV or REVIEW run encounters a configuration refusal, no quarantine scope is active, so the refusal is not recorded and later dispatches in that resumed run can reach the same identity.

When the codex CLI refuses a dispatch before generation with the exact stream captured in the repository (HTTP 400 with error type invalid_request_error and a message saying the model is not supported for a ChatGPT account, and no machine code field), the refusal is classified transient and the dispatch identity is never quarantined, so the next story in the same sprint pays WORKSPACE, preflight, routing and plan to meet the identical refusal again.

Any provider exception raised on the API loop's first iteration — a 429, a 500, a dropped connection — is now stamped with the failure code provider_refused_before_generation, so an ordinary transport outage is recorded and reported as a provider refusal that never happened.

The active story name is held in a process-wide list set once per run_task, so when a sprint runs stories concurrently on its worker threads, a quarantine recorded during one story is stamped with whichever story most recently entered run_task, and the operator-facing record and the routing exclusion reason point at a story whose dispatch was not refused.

When a Codex CLI dispatch learns a pre-generation entitlement refusal and the profile has fallback_models, the runner records the quarantine but returns the refused result without trying an eligible fallback unless the provider prose also matches the old fallback text patterns.

When an API-loop dispatch receives a pre-generation HTTP 400 entitlement refusal such as model_not_found, the API runner raises the SDK exception instead of returning a refusal result, so the dispatch seam never records the quarantine.

When a pre-generation API rejection has error type invalid_request_error and error code context_length_exceeded, it is treated as an account-access denial and quarantines the selected identity for the remainder of the run.
When an API tool loop receives an unclassified HTTP 400 refusal such as context_length_exceeded, the exception escapes before the dispatch seam can emit the required not-quarantined diagnostic.
When provider refusal detail contains a credential-like value, the not-quarantined routing diagnostic writes that value directly to stderr.

When an OpenAI loop dispatch is rejected on its first turn because the model does not accept the tool request shape, the loop now returns a refusal result instead of raising, so the caller's tool-mismatch handler never runs, the capability-mismatch explanation never reaches the operator, and the model is quarantined for the rest of the run.

When a refusal is learned during a pooled dispatch — the review pool or the plan-review pool, which run their agents on their own worker threads — the quarantine record and the routing exclusion reason name the story as 'unknown' rather than the story whose dispatch was refused.

Every exception raised inside a single-shot adapter call — a rate limit, a gateway error, a connection reset, or a local programming error in the request-building code — is recorded with the failure code that names a provider refusal issued before generation, and that code is now also treated as fallback-eligible, so unrelated failures both mislabel the audit trail and trigger a paid fallback dispatch they previously did not.

The branch changes the tool-free OpenAI single-shot exception path to emit refusal evidence and the pre-generation failure code, but the tests never drive an SDK entitlement exception through that adapter path.
The API loop now catches a first-iteration HTTP 400 entitlement exception before the provider-specific re-raise, but no test drives AgentLoopManager or run_api_agent through that exception path.

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
